title: Larkspur Member Dividend on FloodGuard Renewal Payments
content:
Larkspur Mutual pays a member dividend on the renewal payment of a FloodGuard Private Flood Policy according to how many of two other Larkspur lines the customer holds in force: the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy and the Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy (Larkspur Umbrella).

**Dividend rule.** A member dividend reduces the renewal payment by 4 percent of the premium charged for the new term when the customer holds both a HomeGuard policy and a Larkspur Umbrella policy in force; by 2 percent of that premium when the customer holds exactly one of them in force; and by nothing when the customer holds neither.

| HomeGuard Homeowners Policy in force | Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy in force | Member dividend |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 4 percent of the premium charged for the new term |
| Yes | No | 2 percent |
| No | Yes | 2 percent |
| No | No | none |

## Questions the rule answers

**Which records decide the dividend?** The status of the customer's HomeGuard Homeowners Policy and of the customer's Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy in the customer's Larkspur portfolio. A line counts only when a policy of it is in force.

**Is an address named?** The rule asks whether the customer holds a HomeGuard policy in force and whether the customer holds a Larkspur Umbrella policy in force; it names no property address.

**What is the dividend worked out on?** The premium charged for the new term of the flood policy, not the policy fee.

**A hypothetical case.** A customer's premium charged for the new term is 600.00. With a HomeGuard policy and a Larkspur Umbrella policy both in force, the dividend is 4 percent of 600.00, which is 24.00; with only the HomeGuard policy in force, 2 percent, which is 12.00; with neither, none.
